status_summary: On 2025-04-03 DOE reopened, through 2025-04-15, the comment period on three potential National Interest Electric Transmission Corridors selected in December 2024. On 2026-08-12 the Secretary of Energy announced DOE would not advance the Lake Erie-Canada, Southwestern Grid Connector and Tribal Energy Access corridors, stating the designation framework had proved ineffective and had caused confusion and concern in some communities. The announcement does not address state authority or set a plan for future corridors, and a CRS sidebar of 2026-09-04 notes the statutory corridor and FERC backstop siting authority remain in place.

timeline.event: DOE's Grid Deployment Office published a notice reopening, through 2025-04-15, the comment period on the potential Tribal Energy Access, Southwestern Grid Connector and Lake Erie-Canada corridors.

The Secretary of Energy announced DOE would not advance the three proposed corridors (Lake Erie-Canada, Southwestern Grid Connector, Tribal Energy Access), stating the designation process for them should not continue.

title: Respect state authority in National Interest Electric Transmission Corridors
uncertainties: The 2026-08-12 release says nothing explicit about state authority, landowners or future corridors; the match to the Mandate's state-respect aim is inferred from the effect of ending the three designations. The 2024 preliminary list of potential corridors and any FERC rule changes were not separately checked. The researcher searched energy.gov, federalregister.gov and everycrsreport.com; the reviewer queried the Federal Register API for corridor documents since 2025-01-20 and found the 2025-04-03 notice and a 2026-07-09 notice on the draft 2026 National Transmission Needs Study.
